hypothesis: A lightweight zero-initialized EEG/EOG/EMG residual specialist can preserve the original A1 zero v3 raw encoder while allowing channel-specific morphology corrections. Using 4 GPUs with per-replica batch 8 keeps global batch 32 and reduces per-GPU activation pressure.
command: /home/b502/app/anaconda3/envs/l_venv/bin/python3.11 -u tools/run_main_with_protocol_split.py --split-json dataset_protocols/ISRUC/split.json --dataset-preset isruc_A1_concept_film_zero --gpus 4,5,6,7 --per-replica-batch 8 --predict-per-replica-batch 8 --seed 42 --memory-profile balanced --no-preset-batch-clamp --set-env LFTS_EPOCH_ENCODER_VARIANT=v3_channel_specialized_residual_lite --set-env LFTS_PREPROCESS_FILTER_BACKEND=scipy --set-env LFTS_PREPROCESS_FILTER_PROFILE=clinical_canonical --set-env LFTS_PREPROCESS_NORMALIZATION_MODE=recording_robust_zscore --set-env LFTS_RUN_TAG=isruc_A1_chan_spec_residual_lite_4gpu --set-env LFTS_SAVE_PREDICTION_PROBS=1 --set-env LFTS_SAVE_SPLIT_PREDICTION_PROBS=1
interpretation: The residual specialist recovered much of the baseline performance and clearly outperformed stronger adaptive-normalization/channel-calibration variants, but it still remains slightly below A1 zero. This argues against raw-domain normalization as the main bottleneck; channel specialization should be constrained to auxiliary/residual evidence, and the next useful branch should target data quality or channel-specific noise/segment feature auditing rather than stronger normalization.
